question: A mechanically ventilated patient on volume-controlled ventilation (VT 450 mL, RR 14, FiO2 0.5, PEEP 8 cmH2O) has an ABG showing: pH 7.28, PaCO2 58 mmHg, PaO2 95 mmHg. Which adjustment is most appropriate?

answers.text: Increase FiO2 to 0.7 and increase PEEP to 12 cmH2O

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Oxygenation is adequate (PaO2 95 mmHg). Increasing FiO2 and PEEP addresses hypoxia, not the respiratory acidosis (low pH with high PaCO2) seen here.

answers.text: Increase respiratory rate to 18 breaths/min to increase minute ventilation and reduce PaCO2

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The ABG shows respiratory acidosis (pH 7.28, PaCO2 58 mmHg) with adequate oxygenation. Increasing minute ventilation by raising the respiratory rate is the appropriate intervention to increase CO2 elimination and correct the acidosis.

answers.text: Decrease tidal volume to 350 mL to reduce barotrauma

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Reducing tidal volume would further decrease minute ventilation and worsen the existing CO2 retention and respiratory acidosis. It is not appropriate here.

answers.text: Switch to pressure-controlled ventilation with the same settings

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Switching ventilation mode without changing the underlying minute ventilation targets would not correct the respiratory acidosis. Mode switching is not the first-line response.

overallFeedback.feedback: The ABG shows respiratory acidosis with normal oxygenation. The problem is CO2 retention (high PaCO2), not hypoxia. Increasing minute ventilation (RR or VT) is the solution. Review the ABG interpretation and ventilator adjustment section.
Well done. You correctly identified respiratory acidosis from the ABG and chose to increase minute ventilation (via RR) to enhance CO2 clearance — a fundamental ventilator management skill.
